⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the gh-1369 pathology stays reachable via sibling `agent:rework` writers — "no more `agent:rework` stamps on shipped code" overclaims**

The terminal guard itself is well-built (pure leaf, fail-open, probe reuse). But `prTerminalState` is referenced **only** in `js/smAgent.js` — the other machine writers of `agent:rework` still ignore merge state, and each is the same defect class the ticket title names ("Rework-arming stamps agent:rework on already-merged PRs"):

1. `js/postPRReviewComments.js:122-142` — `markForSmStoryRework` (called from `runReworkLeg` at `:2252`): a review leg in flight at merge time concludes REQUEST_CHANGES and stamps `agent:rework` on the now-merged PR/ticket; `rework-on-label` then dispatches a rework leg against shipped code. This is exactly the "leg already flying" race the #1368 family lives in.
2. `js/pushReworkChanges.js:2393` — `rearmNoopRework`: a rework lap concluding no-op on a PR that merged mid-leg re-arms `agent:rework`; the next tick dispatches another dead leg.
3. `js/smAgent.js` `fail_validation` re-arm paths (`:468`, `:472`, `:5276`, `:5288`): a PR that merged while validation was red gets re-armed on the merged head on the next tick.

Each site is one `prHeadAndLabels` + `isTerminalPrState` probe away from closed — the helper already exists and is unit-tested.

**Ask**: either extend the terminal guard to these writers in this PR, or narrow the PR-description claim to the three guarded paths and file the follow-up ticket. As written, "no more `agent:rework` stamps … on shipped code" reads as a class-level fix that is not one yet.

💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: cross-reference the sibling terminal-state helper `isPrBodyFrozen`**

`js/common/pullRequest.js:203-217` already implements a near-sibling decision — `isPrBodyFrozen`: `merged === true` → frozen; state `closed` / `merged` / `completed` → frozen, plus the merge-queue label check. The two contracts legitimately differ (body-freeze vs rework-terminality; ADO `completed` + merge-queue label vs GitHub-REST terminal-only; freeze-by-default vs fail-open), but nothing in either file says so.

A one-line cross-reference in this module's header, e.g. *"sibling: `isPrBodyFrozen` in `pullRequest.js` — different contract (body-freeze, ADO `completed`, merge-queue labels); do not unify without reconciling those and the fail-open doctrine"*, would stop a future dedup pass from silently merging them and flipping one of the semantics (most dangerously, dropping the fail-open behavior the arming paths rely on).

Coverage is uneven across the three guarded writers: the arm suites replay AC1 (merged) **and** AC2 (closed-not-merged), and the unit tests cover `isTerminalPrState('CLOSED', false) === true` — but this reconcile suite replays only `merged: true`.

# Thread: extend the terminal guard to the sibling `agent:rework` writers

**Disposition: fixed — the terminal guard is extended to every sibling `agent:rework` writer in this PR (the class-level fix, not the claim-narrowing escape).**

All three named writer groups now probe terminal state (via `isTerminalPrState`, fail-open) before any write:

1. **`js/postPRReviewComments.js` — `markForSmStoryRework`** (via `runReworkLeg`): a fresh `prIsTerminal(repoInfo, pr.number)` probe (a `github_get_pr` read at *arm* time, not the stale open-PR listing from leg start) exits before `sm_story_rework_triggered`/`agent:rework` land and before `triggerSmIfIdle`. Guard at `runReworkLeg` — the sole production caller of `markForSmStoryRework`.
2. **`js/postPRReviewComments.js` — `rearmReworkOnLinkedIssue`** (via `finishPRAnchoredReview`): same probe gates the REQUEST_CHANGES linked-issue re-arm — this is the third writer the thread's class argument covers, guarded in the same file in the same pass.
3. **`js/pushReworkChanges.js:2421` — `rearmNoopRework`**: `freshTerminalPrState(repoInfo, prNumber)` probes `github_get_pr` at re-arm time (the PR object came from the open-listing — exactly the stale evidence the #1368 race exploited); a terminal PR skips both the label and the no-op comment. `noopLapDecisions` passes `repoInfo` through from its production call site.
4. **`js/smAgent.js` — `conflict_rework` arms** (the gh-683 self-heal at ~`:4702` + the main arm/PR-anchored dispatch): a terminal machine PR exits before the self-heal re-arm, the marker and the report; the state is read from the SAME `github_get_pr` payload that resolves the linked issue — zero extra reads.
5. **`js/smAgent.js` — `fail_validation` re-arms** (linked-issue ~`:5319` + PR-anchored ~`:5331`): `fvPrTerminal` (same already-fetched `prObj`) skips the re-arm entirely — and takes precedence over the empty-lap cap escalation, which cannot summon a human to fix a merged head. The red report stays truthful on a terminal PR ("already MERGED/CLOSED — terminal (gh-1369): nothing to rework") instead of promising "merge aborted, rework re-queued".

The PR-description claim ("no more `agent:rework` stamps on shipped code") is now true class-wide: every machine writer of `agent:rework` in `js/` (`grep -rn "addLabel.*agent:rework" js/`) is either pre-guarded (arm_rework, gh-840 restore, gh-807 reconcile) or guarded by this rework.

Fail-open is preserved everywhere: an unknown/absent state (broken probe, legacy payload, tool-less bridge) keeps the legacy arming semantics — pinned by dedicated probe-failure/legacy-payload tests.

**Tests** (TDD — each writer got a merged/closed/open/probe-failure replay, red before the fix):

- `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js` — suite `smAgent: conflict_rework + fail_validation terminal-PR guard (gh-1369 rework)`: merged + closed-not-merged replays assert no label, no dispatch, no marker/report; open replays pin the legacy arms (conflict → linked-issue `agent:rework`; fail → `#503` linked re-arm); legacy payload without `state` fails open and re-arms as before.
- `js/unit-tests/test_postPRReviewComments.js` — suite `gh-1369 terminal-PR guard on the rework arms`: `runReworkLeg` merged/closed → no labels, no SM kick; open → both labels + kick; probe failure → fail-open; `finishPRAnchoredReview` REQUEST_CHANGES merged → no linked-issue re-arm; open → re-arm lands; probe failure → the legacy quiet no-write.
- `js/unit-tests/test_pushReworkChanges.js` — `rearmNoopRework` merged/closed → silent; open → label + comment; probe failure → fail-open re-arm; `noopLapDecisions` passes the guard through.

# Thread: add the closed-not-merged replay for `reconcile_verdicts`

**Disposition: fixed — the replay is added to the gh-1369 reconcile suite.**

New test in `js/unit-tests/test_smAgent.js`, suite `smAgent: reconcile_verdicts terminal-PR guard (gh-1369)`:

**`AC2 parity — a CLOSED (not merged) PR exits the reconcile too (no label churn, no comment)`** — replays the contradictory-verdict census (newest record REQUEST_CHANGES, so an open PR would strip `pr_approved`) against a PR with `state: 'closed', merged: false`, asserting:

- `capturedPrComments.length === 0` — no reconciliation comment,
- `capturedPrLabelAdds.length === 0` — the reconcile never arms.

The test's comment records the reopen-window rationale from the finding (a closed PR can be reopened; the reconcile deliberately exits during that window and the next tick after reopen self-heals), so the writer-level behavior is now pinned at parity with the arm side (whose AC2 replays closed-not-merged) — a future refactor that special-cases `merged` only now reds the suite.
